    Definitions from Oxford Languages · Learn more
    me·te·or
    /ˈmēdēər,ˈmēdēˌôr/
    Learn to pronounce
    noun
    noun: meteor; plural noun: meteors
    1. a small body of matter from outer space that enters the earth's atmosphere, becoming incandescent as a result of friction and appearing as a streak of light.
      "a meteor streaked across the sky and created a bright fireball"
      h
      Similar:
      falling star
      shooting star
      fireball
      meteorite
      bolide
      meteoroid
      comet
    Origin
    mid 16th century (denoting any atmospheric phenomenon): from modern Latin meteorum, from Greek meteōron, neuter (used as a noun) of meteōros ‘lofty’.
    meteor.
    abbreviation
    1. 1.
      meteorological.
    2. 2.
      meteorology.
    Use over time for: meteor

    People also ask
    What is a simple definition of a meteor?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    A meteor, often called a "shooting star," is the streak of light produced when a small piece of rock or metal from space (a meteoroid) enters Earth's atmosphere at high speed and burns up. It is not actually a star, but rather debris friction heating, which makes it glow. 
    Key facts: 
    • Cause: Friction from passing through the atmosphere.
    • Size: Most are small, often ranging from dust grains to pebbles.
    • Location: Occurs high in the atmosphere, usually between 76–100 km (47–62 miles) up.
    • Survival:
      If a meteor survives the burn and hits the ground, it is called a meteorite.
